Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on iPhone and iPad — network protection, how much the sensor reports, and the tag the host carries in the Microsoft Defender portal.
Silent and zero-touch onboarding are configured elsewhere: SilentOnboard, AutoOnboard, and EnableVPNToggleInApp go in a custom VPN payload whose identifier is com.microsoft.scmx, and device_registration goes in the Microsoft Enterprise SSO extension payload. Only the keys below are read as app configuration.
The human-readable description of this payload. This description appears on the Detail screen.
The human-readable name for the profile payload. The name appears on the Detail screen and doesn’t need to be unique.

The reverse-DNS-style identifier for the payload. This identifier is usually the same as the TopLevel value, with an additional appended component. This string must be unique within the profile. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The payload type, which each payload domain’s reference page specifies.

The globally unique identifier for the payload. The actual content is unimportant, but must be globally unique. In macOS, use ‘uuidgen’ to generate UUIDs. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The version of this specific payload.
The human-readable string containing the name of the organization that provides the profile. This value doesn’t need to match the organization payload value in the enclosing dictionary.

Whether Defender supports devices enrolled through Apple User Enrolment.
Set the string True on a user-enrolment deployment.
This key is a string, not a boolean — Intune’s configuration designer types it as String, and Defender reads it that way.
Whether network protection is active. Set the string false to switch it off.

A string, not a boolean. Network protection also needs the user to open the app once before it initialises, and only one policy should configure it — through MDM or through App Protection Policy, not both.

How open Wi-Fi networks are handled.
In audit mode events reach the Microsoft Defender portal with nothing shown to the user; enable it for the user-facing warning.
Whether users can mark an unsecured network as trusted, or untrust one, from inside the app.

Whether an alert is raised when a user remediates a network problem themselves, such as moving to a safer access point.
This affects alerts only, not device timeline events, and does not apply to open Wi-Fi detection.

Whether network protection runs in privacy mode.
With privacy on, no app data is collected and the user is not asked for consent. With it off, the user is asked to consent to sharing details of the malicious network.

Whether the list of installed apps is withheld from vulnerability assessment.
Set the string False to send the app inventory, which is what makes app vulnerability findings appear for this device.
A string, not a boolean. The default is True on unsupervised devices, so app vulnerability data is off until you set this.

Whether the domain name is left out of phishing reports.
Turn this on and a blocked-site alert says a site was blocked without saying which.
Whether the VPN permission is optional, letting a user finish onboarding without granting it.
Web and network protection run through a local VPN. A user who onboards without granting it appears healthy in the portal while getting none of that protection.
Whether users can send feedback to Microsoft from Help & Feedback inside the app.
The default is false for US Government tenants.

A device tag written to the host record in the Microsoft Defender portal.
Remove the key to remove the tag.
